newsitem.title: USA: Webster Financial to buy DS Bancor.
newsitem.headline: Webster Financial to buy DS Bancor.

text.p: Webster Financial Corp. will acquire DS Bancor Inc., another Connecticut banking company, in a stock deal valued at $137 million, the companies said Tuesday.
Under the definitive agreement, Webster will offer $43 worth of its shares for each D.S. Bancor share in a tax-free pooling of interests.
Waterbury, Conn.-based Webster said it expects to take about $15 million in after-tax charges related to the acquisition, which will boost earnings per share in 1997.
Webster is the parent of Webster Bank, with assets of $3.8 billion and 63 branches throughout Connecticut's central corridor.
The merger will boost Webster's assets to more than $5 billion and its deposits to more than $4 billion, or more than 7 percent of the total deposit market share in Connecticut, it said.
Derby, Conn.-based DS Bancor owns Derby Savings Bank, which has 23 branches mainly in south central Connecticut and assets of $1.3 billion as of June 30.
The deal is expected to close during the first quarter of 1997, subject to approval by both companies' shareholders and regulators.

Webster has an option to buy newly issued shares of Derby common stock equal to an 18.6 percent stake in the company if the deal does not close under certain circumstances. The deal also has mutual provisions for expense reimbursement and a breakup fee under certain conditions.
DS Bancor rose $2 to $40.375 and Webster fell 75 cents to $34.50 early on Nasdaq.
